variables.name: Precipitation
variables.definition: Rain and snow that falls from the sky, averaged per day.
variables.explanation: Precipitation is increasing by about 0.013 mm/day per decade (95% range: -0.155 to +0.184) over 25.7 years. No statistically significant trend was detected (FDR-adjusted p = 0.872). As a rough estimate, if this rate and noise level continue, a record of about 227 years in total would be needed to detect it (we have 25.7). Not significant does not mean no change.
variables.naive_vs_correct: The simple regression and the corrected test agree here.

variables.name: Air temperature (2 m)
variables.definition: The air temperature 2 meters above the ground: the temperature we feel.
variables.explanation: Air temperature (2 m) is increasing by about 0.517 °C per decade (95% range: +0.221 to +0.81) over 26.7 years. This trend is statistically significant (FDR-adjusted p = 0.002).
variables.naive_vs_correct: A simple regression on the raw data misses this trend because the seasonal cycle hides it; after removing the seasonal cycle, the corrected tests find it. Simple methods can also miss real trends.
